name: SDN Host FlatSQL Query Node
description: Generalized engine query node wrapping the storage.flatsql_query_stream hostcall. Method "query": input "query" JSON {"sql":"...","params":[{"t":"i64|f64|str|bool|null|bytes","v":...}]} -> the ALIGNED size-prefixed FlatBuffer result stream passes through VERBATIM on "stream". This is the generic engine query node; data-source/retrieval remains the profile-aware variant (epoch profiles, SDS CAQ request envelopes). Host support: server-only today — storage.flatsql_query_stream is served by the Go node (sdn-server modulert/caps/storage.go, capability storage_query); the SDK BrowserHost storage adapter exposes storage.query/write/delete but not the flatsql stream ops. TRANSITIONAL: flatsql is becoming a component DEPENDENCY with direct in-wasm linkage in a later task; this node uses the hostcall bridge until that lands.

externalInterfaces.description: Host FlatSQL engine-native query streaming (storage.flatsql_query_stream). Served by the Go node today; browser-side flatsql stream ops are not exposed by the SDK BrowserHost storage adapter (server-only until flatsql ships as an in-wasm component dependency).

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON bytes (aligned-binary wire format): {"sql":"..." (required),"params":[{"t":"i64|f64|str|bool|null|bytes","v":...}]}. Tagged params forward verbatim to the host op (decoded by sdn-server decodeTaggedParams).

ALIGNED size-prefixed FlatBuffer stream (schema depends on the query) passed through verbatim from storage.flatsql_query_stream. SDK manifest rules cannot express a generic aligned-binary type, so the port declares the generic flatbuffer ref; runtime frames carry the aligned-binary wire format in their TAB descriptors (requiredAlignment 8), matching data-source/retrieval's rows port.

outputPorts.description: Verbatim aligned size-prefixed FlatBuffer result stream.

methods.description: Executes a FlatSQL query through the transitional storage.flatsql_query_stream hostcall bridge and streams the raw aligned result verbatim.
